scope.goal: The player completes the Qheadache puzzle by moving blocks until the great square reaches the bottom of the board, with the game tracking movements and time and presenting the applicable finish outcome.
scope.start_boundary: The player begins interacting with the puzzle board from the main window that provides a board and menu bar.
scope.success_boundary: The great square is moved to the bottom of the board, all player statistics are frozen, the applicable finish window is shown, and after OK the statistics window is displayed.
in_scope: Board presentation and the movable blocks
Player block selection, deselection, and constrained movement
Tracking block-movement count and elapsed play time
Undo and redo actions available while completing the puzzle
End-of-game detection when the great square reaches the bottom
Selection of Finish Window with Statistics or Simple Finish Window based on recorded statistics
Recording qualifying player statistics through the Finish Window with Statistics
Displaying the statistic window after either finish window is acknowledged
out_of_scope: Opening, saving, or saving-as a game file
Exiting the application
Erasing statistics outside the completion flow
About/help functionality
Operating system portability, Qt platform support, and hardware device requirements
Single-user-per-machine performance constraints

scope.goal: Record and process voucher distribution/sales transactions from MSIU to distributors in the Voucher Management System, including required parties, quantities, automatic voucher allocation, invoice calculation, invoice number generation, cash payment, and directly supported date/numeric validations.
scope.start_boundary: When the VMU User begins a Distribution Transaction for voucher sales from MSIU to a distributor.
scope.success_boundary: The system records the distribution with mandatory distributor, salesman, date, required quantity, automatically allocated vouchers from stock, an automatically calculated invoice amount, cash payment mode, and a generated Distribution Invoice No.
in_scope: Distribution Transactions (Sales from MSIU to Distributor)
Selection of distributor and salesman from masters
Entry of distribution date and required voucher quantity
Automatic voucher allocation from available stock
Grid display of allocated batch numbers, voucher numbers, and validity dates
Automatic invoice amount calculation using wholesale rate/price and quantity sold
Cash payment mode for distribution transactions
Distribution invoice number generation
Date and numeric validation directly specified for distribution transactions
Quick navigation to create missing distributor or salesman master records without closing the current screen
Distribution reporting availability by distributor, salesman, and batch where directly tied to captured distribution information
out_of_scope: Voucher creation/preparation
Claim entry/processing
Voucher sales return processing
Client feedback entry
Security and user-privilege administration
Retail voucher sale to end clients and manual distributor distribution-list entry
Distributor master screen sales-history interactions not part of entering a distribution transaction

evidence.quote: iii. Distribution Transactions (Sales from MSIU to Distributor)

The system will capture the details of voucher sales between MISU sales team and Distributors. During the distribution the system will capture the following details, to make Distribution process easily. With the below details the user can get the details of Distributor-wise and Salesman-wise and Batch No wise sales details as reports.
The mandatory information required during a distribution transaction is mentioned below.
The date of distribution will be current (system) date. But the date of sale can be the past dates. There will be a future date sale validation check available.

scope.goal: Register the submission of claim treatment forms from a Voucher Service Provider (VSP) at the MSIU field office, including master and transaction details, validations, and printing of a submission receipt.
scope.start_boundary: When a VSP submits Claim (Treatment Forms) to the MSIU field office according to the VSP's bi-monthly or monthly payment terms and the field office user begins recording the submission.
scope.success_boundary: When all mandatory claim submission master information and Treatment Form No transaction rows are captured, the transaction form count matches No of Available Forms, and the system prints a receipt document containing the specified header and treatment form details.
in_scope: Capture claim submission master details: VSP Name, Date of submission, No of Mentioned Forms, and No of Available Forms.
Capture claim submission transaction detail: Treatment Form No.
Validate mandatory fields, current submission date, VSP selection from VSP Master, numeric form counts, permitted form-count relationships, and transaction count matching available forms.
Print a claim submission receipt with VSP name, submission date/time, mentioned/available claim counts, and treatment form numbers in the specified header/detail layout.
out_of_scope: Entering individual claim treatment details after claim submission (Claim Entry).
Validating clinical, diagnosis, lab test, drug, amount, patient, referral, or claim-status information for each treatment form.
Claim quarantine, rejection handling, thumb-impression fraud checks, VSP inactivation, or claim amendment.
Claim payment processing or reimbursement.
VSP master, VSP staff master, other master administration, or security/user privilege administration.

rejection and return of forms missing mandatory information
capture of claim master fields
selection of unentered treatment forms and automatic Claim number generation
automatic population and bar-code capture during claim entry
entry of patient, address, doctor, HIV, patient status, referral, claim status, and reason information

scope.goal: Record a Voucher Sales Return when a distributor plans to return vouchers to the MSIU sales team.
scope.start_boundary: A distributor is planning to return vouchers back to the MSIU sales team and the VMU User begins a sales return transaction.
scope.success_boundary: The system captures complete, valid master and transaction details for the returned vouchers and accepts only vouchers that were sold to the selected distributor.
in_scope: Capture sales return master information: Distributor Name, Sales Man Name, Sales Return Date, Sales Return Amount, and Number of vouchers Returned
Capture transaction information for returned vouchers: Batch No and Voucher No
Require all listed master and transaction information
List Distributor Name from Distributor Master
List Sales Man Name from Sales Man Master
Default Sales Return Date to system date and restrict it to less than or equal to system date
Calculate Sales Return Amount from number of vouchers returned multiplied by wholesale rate
Validate that returned vouchers were sold to the selected distributor
Reject returned vouchers that were not sold to the selected distributor
out_of_scope: Voucher Creation / Preparation
Marketing / Sales distribution transactions other than data needed for sales-return validation
Claim Entry / Processing
Client Feed back
Reports (Standard and Customized)
Security and User Privileges

Claim entry and claims processing

Security group or user administration

scope.goal: Acknowledge a Device Alarm: support the Operator through device alarm detection/status, GUI visual and audible presentation, acknowledgment and optional audible silencing, emergency information, unattended notification, and return to normal/icon clearing when the condition is removed.
scope.start_boundary: When the RLCS receives or monitors a device sensor/status meeting configured alarm criteria or otherwise detects a critical or warning alarm condition.
scope.success_boundary: The alarm is presented to the operator, the operator can acknowledge it and optionally silence the audible portion for that device, critical alarm notification occurs even when no operator is logged on, and the alarm icon/status automatically returns to normal when the alarm condition is removed.
in_scope: checking received device sensor status against configured alarm conditions and updating status to indicate an alarm
critical and warning alarm generation for the stated alarm conditions
GUI audible and visual alarm presentation for affected devices
operator acknowledgment of an alarm
silencing the audible portion temporarily for a configurable number of seconds or permanently for that device only
displaying emergency contact information during an alarm condition
critical alarm notification whether or not an operator is logged on
alarm logging for warning and critical alarm events
automatic normal-icon restoration when the alarm condition is removed
critical alarm response during opening or closing operations, including security-checked override advice
out_of_scope: detailed field hardware, I/O card, or pin-configuration design
external system publication intervals and external-server reporting
physical correction or manual field operation of failed devices
alarm cause investigation or alarm escalation procedures not specified in the source
general password/security administration unrelated to alarm acknowledgment or alarm-related override
report generation beyond the specified Alarm Log capability

evidence.quote: Each status received from device sensors shall be checked against alarm conditions for that device sensor and the status will be updated to indicate an alarm.

For alarm status, the GUI shall also issue an audible alarm, and the icon shall be different from the okay status for that device. The visual alarm shall include a change of color for the affected device.
The GUI shall allow the operator to acknowledge an alarm and have the option to silence the audible portion of the alarm for a configurable number of seconds or permanently for that device only.
The RLCS notification to the operator workstation of any critical alarms shall occur within 2 seconds of alarm detection, and shall occur whether or not an operator is logged on to the system.
The alarm icon shall change to the normal status icon automatically when the alarm condition is removed.

Reports unrelated to staff access configuration
Hardware pin configuration and field device mechanics
Detailed network firewall design

in_scope: Management reporting and status-checking privileges

Displaying and modifying Failure Summary Report parameters
Using exported RLCS database data and a COTS reporting tool
Creating the Failure Summary Report from Device Sensor Command Log, Device Command Log, and System Operation Command Log entities where status indicates failure
Formatting report output for GUI display and print/export
Displaying report results, printer setup, report schedule, and print/save controls
Report result and raw-data retention constraints
Report processing non-interference constraint

Field device monitoring, sequencing, and command-execution mechanics unrelated to report generation
System administration and database-table configuration

Problem report generation based on alarms and system status reports, except shared reporting infrastructure
Hardware, controller, network, or low-level I/O design details

scope.goal: Allow a User to create and update a compressed archive in PeaZip 2.7.1, including accessing the Create archive Interface, choosing objects and supported archive options/destination, optionally using volumes, timestamps, encryption, and preserving original objects.
scope.start_boundary: The User initiates archive creation/update through PeaZip, an operating-system context/Send to action, or a supported drag-and-drop archive-creation workflow.
scope.success_boundary: PeaZip creates or updates one or more compressed archive volumes in a supported writable format at the User-selected destination using the User-defined name/options, while the original selected objects remain unchanged at their original storage location.
in_scope: Creating and updating archives from one or more files or archives
Choosing objects included in an archive
Choosing supported compression/archive format and rejecting read-only formats for creation
Choosing destination storage space and archive name
Defining same-name destination behavior
Splitting selected content into User-sized archive volumes
Appending timestamp to archive name
Encrypting created/updated archives with password and optional keyfile
Preserving source objects during archive creation/update
Access paths to the Create archive Interface from File, Browser, toolbar Add, context menu Add, and Send to separate archives
Drag-and-drop workflows that populate or update archive creation when supported by the format
Archive-creation layout keyboard shortcuts and creation-related settings
out_of_scope: Archive extraction/decompression as a primary workflow
Browsing, selection sorting, system management tools, or non-archiving file utilities
Secure deletion, duplicate/checksum tools, comparison, benchmark, split/join outside archive creation, and hex/info tools
Command generation/saving and execution-monitoring requirements except as unrelated general capabilities
Installation, operating environment, hardware, and nonfunctional requirements not specific to archive creation
Settings unrelated to archive creation formats/defaults or creation parameters

scope.goal: Allow a User to extract/decompress the contents of a selected supported archive into a user-selected folder or location using PeaZip’s extraction interface or supported extraction entry points, while preserving the source archive and enforcing encryption authentication.
scope.start_boundary: The User selects one or more supported archives or opens PeaZip’s extraction interface through the toolbar, Browser menu, context menu, operating-system Send to menu, or a directly related extraction control.
scope.success_boundary: The selected archive’s contents are extracted and, when needed, decompressed into the User-selected storage location/name according to extraction options; the original archive remains unchanged at its original location.

General error/help behavior applicable when wrong extraction data or settings are supplied
out_of_scope: Archive creation and updating

Password or keyfile generation
File browsing unrelated to extraction
File and system management utilities unrelated to extraction
Feature settings customization not specific to extraction
Graphical progress display as a separate feature

evidence.quote: Users can use PeaZip for decompressing the contents of a selected (by them) compressed archive and extract them in a folder. Name and storage space of the folder in the computer system, are up to users to decide.

For the procedure of decompression and extraction to be completed, it is necessary that the selected archive is of one of the supported for extraction by PeaZip formats. In case the selected archive is encrypted, user must know and insert password and (if there is one) keyfile in order to have access to the archives contents (for browsing or extracting them).

Decompression/Extraction function is set off and defined in extraction window (which is also going to be referred as extraction interface). Users can get access to this window in one of the following ways:

In Extraction window (Extraction Interface), users are given the ability of choosing the storage space in the computer system in which the file that will contain the extracted from the compressed archive objects will be saved, of choosing name for this file (as well as defining what should happen in case of existence of a homonym file or archive in the selected storage space) and of inserting password and (if needed) keyfile, in case the archive is encrypted (locked).

This feature is one of the most important for users, because not only does it offer access to the contents of a compressed, in one of the supported by PeaZip formats, archive, but it allows extraction of those contents in non-compressed format too, in order to be used according to users’ desires.

scope.goal: Generate provider reimbursement reports for processed voucher claims and send them to the MSIU Admin team to arrange provider payments.
scope.start_boundary: After claims have been submitted, entered, validated, and classified according to their payment/claim status, the field office user initiates reimbursement report generation based on each VSP's agreed payment terms.

Reports on claims per provider and reports summarising all providers
Quarterly provider and all-provider summary reimbursement-related reports
Claim status reporting for selected VSPs
Report access and printing controlled by user privileges
Claim amount data sources used in reimbursement calculation
Medical and statistical reports listed in the Reports section (syndromes, clients/partners, documentation quality, provider comparison, time trends)
out_of_scope: Creating vouchers
Distributing or selling vouchers
Entering claims from paper treatment forms
Performing medical treatment or collecting thumbprints
Making the actual bank transfer or payment
Investigating and clearing conspicuous claims by VMU management
Designing undefined customized reports beyond the listed standard reports

target.name: Generate Treatment Quality and Trend Reports

scope.goal: Generate Treatment Quality and Trend Reports
scope.start_boundary: When the MSIU Field Office User requests a treatment-quality or trend report from the Reports module after claim data has been entered.

in_scope: Required standard reports specified in the Reports module

Syndromes treated and patient population information
Primary clients and notified partners
Documentation, algorithm-compliance, treatment-alteration, treatment-error, and treatment-behaviour indicators

Quarterly and half-yearly time-trend reports
Report capability for analytical, medical, and statistical reports
Group-level View and Print permission enforcement for reports
out_of_scope: Financial payment/withholding reports unless they are required only as separate Reports-module entries
Report layouts, filters, sorting, export formats, and calculation rules because they may be designed later or are unspecified
Voucher creation, marketing/sales, voucher sales return, client feedback, and payment execution
Claim submission and data-entry mechanics except where entered claim data supplies report content
User-group creation and privilege administration

scope.goal: Maintain distributor master records, including capture, validation, update, constrained deletion, activation/deactivation, viewing/printing master and sales-history information, and use/quick creation of distributor records from distribution transactions.
scope.start_boundary: When the VMU User opens or uses the Marketing / Sales module’s Distributor Master Information screen, or uses distributor master information/navigation during a distribution transaction.
scope.success_boundary: Distributor master data is captured with required fields and uniqueness/duplicate handling, records can be added, edited, deleted only when child records do not exist, activated/deactivated, viewed/printed as permitted, and distributor records can be selected or quickly created from distribution transactions without closing the transaction.
in_scope: Distributor master information fields and mandatory-field rules
Unique distributor code and duplicate ID/name handling
Geographic address content and address-level master tables
Printing distributor master details
Viewing distributor sales history and selecting a distributor from the grid
Sales-history report fields, header, and login-permission-controlled printing
Screen-level New, Edit, Delete, and Active/Deactivate options
Viewing distributor purchase and sales details
Selection of distributor from Distributor Master during distribution transactions
Quick navigation to distributor master from distribution transactions
out_of_scope: Voucher creation/preparation
Salesman master maintenance except where jointly referenced by distribution-transaction navigation
Distribution transaction voucher allocation, invoice calculation, payment mode, and date validation beyond distributor selection or quick navigation
Voucher sales return processing
Claim entry/processing and VSP maintenance
Client feedback entry
General reports outside distributor master and distributor sales history
Security/user-group administration

evidence.quote: i. Distributor Master Information
The system will capture the master details of every distributor so that the users can get the details of any distributor and sales details at any time.

There will be an option for doing the following at every screen.
New (adding new records)
Edit (updating available records)
Delete (deleting will be allowed only if no child records are created)
Name of the distributor (Selecting from Distributor Master)

Suppose the distributor or salesman name is not available in the system, then the system has a provision to navigate quickly to its master screen and enter the new Distributor and Salesman details, without closing the present screen.

scope.goal: Maintain Voucher Service Provider (VSP) master records, including service provider identification, addresses and facility attributes, status, payment terms, permission-controlled maintenance, and related claim-status visibility in the Voucher Management System.
scope.start_boundary: An allowed VMU User begins creating, viewing, modifying, deleting, activating, or inactivating a VSP master record or its payment terms.
scope.success_boundary: The VSP record is saved or maintained with required data, valid referenced master values, a system-generated VSP code, duplicate-name handling, applicable status changes, and controlled payment terms; Active VSPs are available for data entry and all VSPs for reports as specified.
in_scope: VSP master information fields and mandatory fields
Automatic VSP code generation
Duplicate VSP name confirmation
Address and facility/reference master selection with quick master entry
VSP Active/In-Active status management, including automatic inactivation after the fraud threshold and MSIU-management-controlled reactivation
Payment terms and period-specific fee details
Permission-controlled add, modify, and delete of VSP master information including payment terms
Viewing claim status for a selected VSP
out_of_scope: Distributor and salesman master records
Voucher creation/preparation
Distribution/sales transactions
Voucher sales return
Detailed claim form submission and claim entry beyond VSP claim-status view
VSP Staff Master maintenance as a separate target
Clinical treatment masters and treatment matrix
Client feedback
General report definitions other than availability of all VSPs for report purposes
General user group administration except its effect on VSP permissions

scope.goal: Allow a VMU User to review the claim status of a selected voucher service provider (VSP).
scope.start_boundary: The VMU User selects or opens a VSP and requests to view that provider's claim status from the VSP screen.
scope.success_boundary: The system presents the selected VSP's claim status details, including the report header, claim status details when necessary, and cumulative prior-payment amount footer.
in_scope: Accessing claim status from the VSP screen for a selected VSP
Displaying the selected VSP name as report header and claim details in the details part

Understanding statuses and reason information associated with rejected or quarantined claims shown in the claim-status view

Processing payments or reimbursements
Generating monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly, or other standard reports
General VSP activation/inactivation management not required to review claim status

scope.goal: Define source-grounded requirements for an Operator to close a reversible-lane entrance, including command authorization and confirmation, safety checks, closing device sequence and timing, monitoring, halt/resume, alarms, overrides, logging, and initial normal-mode closing operations.
scope.start_boundary: An authorized Operator requests or confirms a closing operation for a reversible-lane entrance through the RLCS GUI or scheduled command sequence.
scope.success_boundary: The RLCS executes the required closing sequence, closes or otherwise positions the listed devices in the specified order and direction, updates/displays status, and the entrance or facility reaches the intended closed configuration without unresolved safety-screening failure or unknown/improper closure-device status.
in_scope: Operator GUI command entry and confirmation for closing sequences
Authorization, security level, workstation, MCU mode, and command-control restrictions
Integrity checks, status checks, safety rules, interlocks, and safety screening before and during closing execution
Generic F.4 closing order and directional sequencing for CMS, entrance pop-ups, wrong-way pop-ups, and barrier gate
Response-time windows, sequential execution, halt, hold, and resume behavior during closing
Status monitoring/display/database update and critical alarm handling during closing
Device override behavior when needed to continue a closing operation
Device and system-operation command logs for closing operations
Initial normal-mode Sequence #2 and Sequence #4 scheduled closing operations
out_of_scope: Opening-sequence-only ordering requirements except where they define opposite-direction safety constraints or are subordinate steps in configured closing sequences
External traveler/public data dissemination and external-system reporting details
Hardware pin configuration and controller replacement details
COTS report formatting unrelated to closing commands
System Administrator database configuration except where it affects command authorization, safety rules, or scheduled closing
Physical roadway construction or site adaptation

unresolved_issues.issue: The target is named 'Close a Reversible-Lane Entrance,' but the source includes both a generic entrance-closing sequence in F.4 and facility-wide scheduled closing sequences in F.11. The inventory retains both because F.4 defines device order and F.11 supplies initial configured closing operations; implementers should distinguish single-entrance closure from full-facility closing.

F.10 states unknown or improper closure-device status anywhere 'may' terminate a device-closing command, while other clauses mandate abort/halt for unknown status or specify exact closing halt conditions. The modal difference is preserved rather than converting 'may' into a mandatory halt.

Unattended operations (F.12) describe behavior when no operator is logged on. While relevant to scheduled closing sequences, the primary actor is the Operator, creating a scope ambiguity regarding whether unattended behaviors are strictly in scope for this use case or a separate system capability.

scope.goal: Configure Operational Schedules
scope.start_boundary: An authorized System Administrator accesses the GUI Configuration option to create or modify system configuration data for scheduled operations.
scope.success_boundary: Valid System Operation Command Schedule data and associated configuration data are stored in the RLCS database; conflicting or redundant entries are identified before storage.
in_scope: System Administrator authorization for scheduled operations
Administratively restricted GUI Configuration access
Display and modification of non-log database tables that define scheduled operations
Pre-storage analysis and notification of conflicting or redundant configuration entries
System Operation Command Schedule attributes: schedule ID, mode, start day/time, end day/time, frequency, and referenced operational command, device command macro, or device command
Support for advance recurring schedules and immediate-execution schedule entries
Schedule-to-mode, schedule-to-agency, and schedule-to-command relationships
out_of_scope: Runtime execution and monitoring of schedules
Operator confirmation of scheduled commands
Audible alarms for unattended operations
General authentication and authorization unrelated to schedule configuration
Report generation from schedules
Device-level hardware I/O pin configuration
Changing device command rules (requires simulator testing and database upload)

scope.goal: Allow Field Maintenance Staff to diagnose a failed device at the sensor level through the GUI, including viewing sensor data, issuing diagnostic commands, and accessing relevant logs, subject to Field Maintenance Staff mode, workstation, and system-mode-change restrictions.
scope.start_boundary: A Field Maintenance Staff member logs on to the RLCS Application from an authorized workstation (FCU, remote dial-in, or maintenance building) and invokes the GUI diagnostic capability for a failed device.
scope.success_boundary: The system presents sensor-level diagnostic information for the selected failed device or executes the requested supported diagnostic function, subject to the user's authorized mode and workstation.
in_scope: GUI diagnostic screen for failed devices at sensor level
Single-device detail display showing all sensor data
Diagnostic commands that run diagnostics on devices or controllers

Prohibition on Field Maintenance Staff changing system mode

Logon and authentication for Field Maintenance Staff
Viewing alarm, device command, and maintenance logs
Remote dial-in access for Field Maintenance Staff
Safety screening of commands issued by Field Maintenance Staff
MCU Auto mode requirement for processing commands
out_of_scope: Physical repair, hardware replacement, or manual field-device operation
Root-cause analysis beyond presenting diagnostics or sensor data
Operator normal-mode command control
General reporting and status-checking capabilities of other user classes
Inventing authentication or remote-session workflows not specified in the source
System configuration changes (restricted to System Administrator)

target.name: Initialize a Newly Online Control Unit

scope.goal: Initialize a newly online Control Unit so it is identified, its required cards and associated device sensors are checked and initialized, control-system integrity is verified using the referenced integrity mechanism, specified tables/configuration data are initialized, startup completes within 30 seconds when all checks are OK, and the unit begins monitoring devices and reporting current status to the FCU or TSU at the configured current-mode rate.
scope.start_boundary: When a workstation or intelligent controller at the FCU or DCU comes online, or when the RLCS software in the field starts.
scope.success_boundary: The Control Unit and associated device sensors have been identified and initialized; required cards, control-system integrity, tables, and non-volatile configuration items have been checked or initialized as specified; when everything is OK startup has completed within 30 seconds; and the unit monitors all devices and sends current status to the FCU or TSU every 2 seconds or at the rate specified in the System Control Parameters for the current mode.
in_scope: Online identification of a workstation or Control Unit and all associated device sensors
Field RLCS software self-identification by reading cabinet ID
Verification that all cards required in the unit are present and working properly
Initialization of each Control Unit and device sensor as identified
Control-system integrity check during startup
Initialization of specified tables
Replicated Control Unit non-volatile, non-removable configuration data
Startup duration limit when all checks are OK
Post-startup monitoring of all devices
Post-startup current-status reporting to FCU or TSU every 2 seconds or at the current-mode configured rate
One-way hash support for the referenced control-system integrity mechanism
Failure response when non-volatile memory item verification fails
out_of_scope: Routine opening and closing sequence execution after startup
Processing ordinary GUI commands after startup

evidence.quote: 3.2.2.6 Identify units and Initialize all Devices
3.2.2.6.1 When each workstation and control unit (workstation or intelligent controller at the FCU or DCU) comes online, the system shall identify it and all its associated device sensors.
3.2.2.6.2 The RLCS software shall initialize each control unit and device sensor as it is identified.

3.2.2.6.2.1 RLCS Software Startup PROCESS: The RLCS software in the field shall first identify the its unit when it starts, by reading the cabinet id. The RLCS software will then proceed to make sure that all the cards required in that unit are present and working properly. The RLCS software will do a control system integrity check ( see requirement 3.0.9) and initialize all the specified tables. If everything is OK the start up process shall not exceed 30 seconds. The RLCS software shall then monitor all the devices and send the current status to the FCU or TSU every 2 seconds (or at the rate specified in the System Control Parameters for the current mode).

Control Unit Non-Volatile Memory

scope.goal: Monitor the status of the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System facility and field devices via the Graphical User Interface.
scope.start_boundary: The RLCS is operating and displaying facility/device status information, whether or not the operator is logged on; when logged on, the operator may access monitoring displays according to security level.

in_scope: Facility geographic and status display

Field device, sensor, and controller monitoring
Single-device and device-category detail status displays
Alarm visual/icon/color indication, audible alarm notification, emergency contact display, and operator alarm acknowledgment/silencing
Display of active overrides and devices lacking rules protection
Unattended status monitoring and display
Operator-facing performance requirements for status display, alarm detection/notification, and status circulation
out_of_scope: Issuing device control commands to change device state

Creating, scheduling, or exporting reports beyond status-related viewing capabilities

Hardware/controller design and physical pin configuration
External-server status updates for external systems

rejection of inputs from other systems on the published roadway-state interface
out_of_scope: RLCS operator login or command control
field device monitoring/control and opening/closing sequences
secure remote dial-in two-way maintenance access
report generation from the RLCS database
logical database design and general internal database management

scope.goal: Allow a System Administrator to revise device command safety rules used by the RLCS to validate control commands.
scope.start_boundary: When the System Administrator accesses the GUI Configuration/device rules option to change device command safety rules.
scope.success_boundary: After rule changes are analyzed, tested in the Simulator environment, and uploaded as a new database version to production, the secured revised rules are available for command validation/safety screening.
in_scope: System Administrator access and modification of the Device Rules database table
Additional password protection for configuring device rules
Conflict/redundancy analysis before modified database entries are stored
Testing device command rule changes in the Simulator environment
Uploading a new database version to production after testing
Encryption, non-volatile replication, and integrity protection for revised device rule data
Use of revised secured safety rules in validation/safety screening of processed control commands
Maintenance of the Device Rules attributes and its defined Device relationship
out_of_scope: General operator command control unrelated to rule revision
Field device hardware replacement or I/O card pin configuration
Routine report generation unrelated to rule revision
Creating or managing staff accounts except where tied to System Administrator configuration authorization
Password aging and username/password length policy administration not specific to device-rule revision
Operational sequence ordering requirements unrelated to safety screening execution

scope.goal: Define Customer-facing requirements to register a JTVauctions account through the short and full registration process.
scope.start_boundary: A customer begins registration on Registration Page 1 by entering the minimum account and payment information needed to create an account and bid.
scope.success_boundary: The customer account is created after required validation and Terms of Use acceptance, either via the short process or by completing Registration Page 2 with shipping and email preferences, and the registration confirmation messaging/email is triggered.
in_scope: Two-page registration process
Registration Page 1 minimum user and payment information
Default payment method collection during registration
Terms of Use acceptance required before proceeding
Short registration completion and browse/sign-in routing
Registration Page 2 membership, billing/shipping, shipping preference, and email preference collection
Duplicate-account, email uniqueness, negative-file, and email-blacklist restrictions
Registration confirmation email, cookie, and safe-sender instructions
out_of_scope: Sign-in processing after account creation, except registration routing back to the sign-in page and specified post-registration return routing
Account editing functionality after registration
Bidding, QuickBid, SmartBid, auction monitoring, watch lists, and auction payment/checkout after winning

scope.goal: Define Customer-facing product browsing and searching capabilities for JTVauctions.com, including home-page canned search entry points, category/search-result navigation, product-module presentation, sorting/pagination/views, keyword/attribute/wildcard search, result routing, no-results behavior, drill-down navigation, and navigation to product details where directly tied to browsing/search.
scope.start_boundary: A customer accesses JTVauctions.com, uses header/menu/navigation controls, enters a search, or clicks a category or canned-search entry point to browse auction products.
scope.success_boundary: The customer can browse active auction products through categories and navigation, search active items by supported attributes and description text, view dynamically updated result modules, sort/page through results, choose supported views, and reach the appropriate product details or no-results page.
in_scope: Home page canned search entry points relevant to browsing/search
Category browse and search result pages
Customer-facing product modules on browse/result pages
Sorting, pagination, page-size, and view controls
Customer-facing keyword, attribute, and wildcard search
Search result routing for one match, multiple matches, and no results
Endeca or Endeca-like customer navigation and drill-down
Breadcrumbs, left navigation, multi-category product placement, image eligibility, and closed-item behavior in customer browse/search contexts
SEO landing pages for browsing
out_of_scope: Auctioneer administrative inventory search and scheduling pages

Bid placement mechanics, SmartBid/QuickBid processing, bid confirmation, payment, checkout, shipping, and auction closure logic except where controls or restrictions appear within customer browse/search pages
Registration, sign-in, account management, and order processing
Auction Admin reporting and analytics implementation
Second-chance auctions
Phase 2 and future enhancements such as Buy It Now, international functionality, SMS, chat, third-party vendors, and networked auction sites

scope.goal: Define Customer-facing requirements for completing checkout and payment after winning JTVauctions auctions, including accepted payment methods, automated credit-card processing, PayPal/Amazon Payments winner payment flows, payment deadlines, and resulting account/order constraints.
scope.start_boundary: When an auction ends and the system identifies the Customer as winner and checks the winner's payment method, or when the Customer accesses the Returning Winners Payments page to pay unpaid winnings.
scope.success_boundary: The Customer completes the applicable credit-card, PayPal, or Amazon Payments checkout process; an APM checkout returns the Customer to the Thank You page, or the Customer elects Checkout Later within the stated payment window.
in_scope: Accepted payment methods
Credit-card automated order processing after winning
PayPal and Amazon Payments winner notification and payment instructions
Winnings Alert visibility and navigation to Returning Winners Payments
Links to Returning Winners Payments from specified site pages
Returning Winners Payments page content and Customer actions
Shipping-method selection during APM checkout
PayPal redirect and Amazon Payments widget checkout behavior
Checkout Later DIV behavior
Payment deadline, cancellation, Hold, reporting, and account-status consequences
Post-checkout Thank You page
Auction-processing payment handling that constrains Customer checkout
out_of_scope: Auction Administrator configuration of payment or shipping settings
Auctioneer scheduling and auction management
CSR workflows except account constraints directly triggered by Customer non-payment
2nd-Chance offer acceptance flow
International shipping Phase 2 enhancements
Future alternative payment methods beyond PayPal and Amazon Payments
Underlying database, inventory import, tax-processing, and implementation details

evidence.quote: The site will accept credit cards (Visa, MC, American Express, and Discover), PayPal, and Amazon Payments.
When an auction ends, the system will check the winner’s payment method type in their registration data, and proceed according to payment method.
Upon completing the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the user will be returned to a Thank You page, which uses the global header and footer, and a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.

Orders won with credit card as the MOP should charge that credit card as soon as the auction is 
over, before being accumulated into the combined order.

requirements.text: The site shall accept Customer payment using Visa, MasterCard, American Express, Discover, PayPal, and Amazon Payments.

evidence.quote: The site will accept credit cards (Visa, MC, American Express, and Discover), PayPal, and Amazon Payments.

requirements.text: When an auction ends, the system shall check the winning Customer's payment method type in registration data and proceed according to that payment method.

evidence.quote: When an auction ends, the system will check the winner’s payment method type in their registration data, and proceed according to payment method.

requirements.text: When a Customer who stores credit-card information wins an auction, the system shall automatically process the order and send the winner an order confirmation email.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer has stored credit-card information and wins an auction"}]

evidence.quote: Users who store their credit card information will have an automated checkout process. Upon winning an auction, the system will automatically process the order and send the winner an order confirmation email.

requirements.text: When a Customer's default payment method is PayPal or Amazon Payments, the Customer shall experience a checkout process different from the automated credit-card process.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"PayPal or Amazon Payments is the Customer's default payment method in registration information"}]

evidence.quote: Users with PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default payment method in their registration information will experience a different checkout process.

requirements.text: Upon winning an auction, a PayPal or Amazon Payments Customer shall receive a “Congratulations Winner!” email instructing the Customer to sign in and provide payment information.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer whose default payment method is PayPal or Amazon Payments wins an auction"}]

evidence.quote: Upon winning an auction, these users will receive a “Congratulations Winner!” email. This email will instruct them to sign in and provide their payment information.

requirements.text: When a PayPal or Amazon Payments Customer has unpaid auction winnings, the Customer shall see a highly visible “Winnings Alert” in place of the normal promotional text bar.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer has PayPal or Amazon Payments as default MOP and has unpaid auction winnings"}]

evidence.quote: Customers who have PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default Method of Payment (MOP) and who have unpaid auction winnings, will see a “Winnings Alert” in place of the normal promotional text bar. This text bar should be highly visible.

requirements.text: The system shall identify and serve the Winnings Alert to the Customer through a cookie, through the “pay now” link in the Responsys winner notification email, or because the Customer signed in.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer is a PayPal or Amazon Payments Customer with unpaid winnings"}]

evidence.quote: Customers will be identified and served the text bar either via a cookie, or via the “pay now” link in the winner notification email from Responsys, or because they signed in.

requirements.text: The Customer shall make payment within seven days, exactly 168 hours, of the auction’s closing date/time.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Winner is required to pay for auction winnings"}]

evidence.quote: Payment must be made within seven days (168 hours) of the auction’s closing date/time.

requirements.text: The winner notification email shall notify the Customer that Users who fail to complete transactions may have their accounts suspended.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer receives the winner notification email"}]

evidence.quote: The email will include a notification that users who fail to complete transactions may have their accounts suspended.
evidence.visual_region_description: Account suspension notice in payment deadline bullet

requirements.text: If an Amazon or PayPal order is not paid within 168 hours of being won, the system shall cancel the order and place the item into “Hold” status.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Amazon or PayPal order remains unpaid 168 hours after the auction is won"}]

evidence.quote: Orders not paid for with Amazon or PayPal (with 168 hours of being won) will be cancelled, and the item placed into a “Hold” status.

requirements.text: Cancelled unpaid Amazon or PayPal orders shall count as churned auctions in reporting.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Amazon or PayPal order is cancelled after non-payment"}]

evidence.quote: These cancelled orders will count as churned auctions in the reporting.
evidence.visual_region_description: Reporting consequence within unpaid order bullet

requirements.text: When the Customer clicks the “Winnings Alert” link, the system shall take the Customer to the “Returning Winners Payments” page.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer clicks the Winnings Alert link"}]

evidence.quote: When the user clicks on the “Winnings Alert” link, they will be taken to the “Returning Winners Payments” page.

requirements.text: The site shall provide a link to the Returning Winners Payments page from My Account, My Watch List, My Current Bids, My Bid History, and the Safe Shopping Guarantee page.

evidence.quote: A link to this page will also be provided on various other pages, including the My Account page, My Watch List, My Current Bids, My Bid History, and the Safe Shopping Guarantee page.

requirements.text: The Returning Winners Payments page shall display a personalized “Welcome Back Winner!” message.

evidence.quote: A personalized Welcome Back Winner! Message.

requirements.text: The Returning Winners Payments page shall display its specified instructional paragraph, including the XX item count, $XXX.XX total, reason involving PayPal or Amazon Payments default method, and instruction to choose items, shipping method, and payment type.

evidence.quote: “Congratulations! You've won XX items for a total of $XXX.XX. We've included a list of these items below. You are seeing this message because you have chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as your default method of payment. Please complete your transaction(s)  by choosing which items you want to pay for right now, then a shipping method, and finally a payment type. As always, thank you for participating  at JTVauctions.com!
evidence.visual_region_description: Instructional paragraph at top of page 130

requirements.text: The Checkout Later DIV shall include a “Return to Payments” link that closes the DIV and re-enables the page links.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Checkout Later DIV is displayed"}]

evidence.quote: This DIV will also include two buttons: a “Return to Payments” link (which closes the DIV and re-enables the page links)

requirements.text: The Checkout Later DIV shall include a “JTVauctions Homepage” link that takes the Customer to the home page.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Checkout Later DIV is displayed"}]

evidence.quote: and a “JTVauctions Homepage” link, which takes the user to the home page.

requirements.text: Orders won with a credit card as method of payment shall charge that credit card as soon as the auction is over, before accumulation into the combined order.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer wins an auction with credit card as MOP"}]

evidence.quote:
Orders won with credit card as the MOP should charge that credit card as soon as the auction is 
over, before being accumulated into the combined order.

requirements.text: Orders won with PayPal or Amazon Payments shall be placed in Hold status until payment is received.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer wins an auction using PayPal or Amazon Payments"}]

evidence.quote:
Orders won with an alternative payment method, i.e. PayPal or Amazon Payments, will be 
placed in a Hold status until payment is received.

requirements.text: If payment for a PayPal or Amazon Payments order is not received within 168 hours, the item order shall be cancelled.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Payment is not received within 168 hours of an APM auction win"}]

evidence.quote:
If payment is not received within 168 hours, the item order will 
be cancelled.

requirements.text: Customers with unpaid auction winnings greater than 7 days old shall not be allowed to bid.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer has unresolved unpaid auction winnings greater than 7 days old"}]

evidence.quote:
Customers / Bidders who have unresolved (i.e., unpaid) auction winnings greater than 7 days 
old will not be allowed to bid.

requirements.text: When a PayPal or Amazon Payments Customer allows an order to expire, the system shall automatically lock the account by putting it into Review Status, and only a Customer Service Representative shall be able to unlock it.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"PayPal or Amazon Payments order expires unpaid"}]

evidence.quote:
The system will automatically lock accounts when a PayPal or 
Amazon Payments customer allows their order(s) to expire, thus putting the account into a 
"Review Status." These "Review Status" accounts can only be "unlocked" by a customer 
service representative.

requirements.text: A Customer shall not be able to unlock an expired-order Review Status account by paying because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"APM order has expired and account is in Review Status"}]

evidence.quote:
Customers cannot unlock the account themselves by paying for the 
orders, because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours)

requirements.text: A Customer subject to the escalation policy shall not bid again until a Customer Service Representative removes the account from Review Status.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer becomes subject to escalation policy"}]

evidence.quote:
When an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy, they cannot bid again 
until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status.

requirements.text: The only way for a Customer to have an escalated account removed from Review Status shall be by updating the account with a credit card.
requirements.conditions: [{"condition":"Customer is subject to escalation policy and account is in Review Status"}]

evidence.quote:
The only way for a 
customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with 
a credit card.

requirements.text: After escalation, a Customer may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until the order cancel rate falls below 10%.

scope.goal: Allow a registered Customer to view and manage membership account information, billing/shipping addresses, shipping preferences, payment methods, and email preferences through the My Account and My Account Edit pages.
scope.start_boundary: The customer opens the My Account page or a linked My Account Edit page while using the customer-facing auction site.
scope.success_boundary: The customer can review current account settings, make permitted edits through the relevant edit page, save or cancel changes, and be returned to the My Account page with the requested settings updated when saved.
in_scope: My Account page display of customer information, addresses, shipping preferences, payment methods, email preference link, Returning Winners Payments link, and personalized greeting
My Account Edit Page 1 for membership account information
My Account Edit Page 2 for billing and shipping addresses
My Account Edit Page 3 for payment methods and stored credit cards
My Account Edit Page 4 for transactional email preferences and newsletter subscription link
Customer save and cancel navigation behavior
Address validation for new and edited addresses
Payment-method explanatory text and payment-method-specific restrictions visible to the customer
out_of_scope: Initial registration process and duplicate-account checks
Auction browsing, bidding, watch lists, bid history, and current bids pages except account-page links explicitly specified
Winner checkout and PayPal/Amazon payment processing beyond links or payment-method settings shown in account management
Auction Administrator, Auctioneer, CSR, or Help Desk account-management actions
Customer service-initiated account suspension, review status, deactivation, password reset, or account notes
Reporting, inventory, auction scheduling, and site administration
Phase 2 enhancements such as international address formats and member location features

target.name: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status

scope.goal: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status
scope.start_boundary: A registered customer views current auctions, items they are bidding on or watching, their prior bid activity, or auctions that have recently ended.
scope.success_boundary: The customer can determine the live status and time remaining for current auctions and review the outcome/history of past auctions through the relevant customer-facing pages and linked item details.
in_scope: Customer monitoring of currently bid-on items (My Current Bids)
Customer monitoring of watched items (My Watch List)
Customer review of prior bids, won items, and lost items (My Bid History)
Customer viewing recently ended auctions for 24 hours (Recently-Ended Auctions)
Dynamic current date/time, countdown timers, current high bid, and bid status indicators
Links from monitoring/history pages to product details bidding pages
Customer access from relevant customer-facing pages to returning winner payment links for unpaid won items
Customer email notifications for outbid, winner, and shipping events
out_of_scope: Auction Admin reporting pages for internal management
Auctioneer scheduling or editing auctions
Customer Service account management
Checkout payment processing beyond links/status shown in monitoring pages
Phase 2 international functionality, SMS notifications, bidder chat, or future auction models
