4.4.4.3.1h.

candidate_decisions.reason: C-only restricted-TQ prohibition duplicates B:D019 and is source-supported; mapped to the same confirmed row.

evidence.quote: (a) A track with TQ ≤ e... This prohibition does not apply to new local real-time tracks... e = 4(2-6, 1) "Restricted TQ". Tracks with TQ less than or equal to e are not eligible for correlation, except for new local real-time tracks

candidate_decisions.reason: C-only E/C conflict test prohibition duplicates B:D019 and is source-supported; mapped to the same confirmed row.

evidence.quote:
(b)  Tracks of different E/C, and tracks with existing E/C 
conflicts.

candidate_decisions.reason: C-only simulated/live test prohibition duplicates B:D019 and is source-supported; mapped to the same confirmed row.

evidence.quote:
(c)  Simulated tracks with live tracks, and live tracks 
with simulated tracks.

candidate_decisions.reason: C-only ID-conflict operator alert duplicates B:D036 and is source-supported; mapped to the same confirmed row.

evidence.quote: (2) If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted. The purpose of this alert is to cue the operator to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID... (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report... (c) Confirm the restriction... (d) Conduct voice coordination...

candidate_decisions.reason: C-only post-ID-resolution decorrelation test duplicates B:D037 and is source-supported; mapped to the same confirmed row.

evidence.quote:
(3)  If the above actions result in resolution of the ID 
conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in 
accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except

candidate_decisions.reason: C-only manual correlation capability duplicates B:D012 and is source-supported; mapped to the same confirmed row.

evidence.quote: A manual capability shall be provided to initiate the correlation of any two tracks... except that two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.

candidate_decisions.reason: C-only response-to-correlation-request requirement duplicates B:D013 and is source-supported; mapped to the same confirmed row.

evidence.quote:
C2 JUs shall perform correlation 
tests in response to correlation requests from other units in accordance with 
the requirements of paragraph 4.7.3.2.

scope.goal: Manage Track Identity Classification
scope.start_boundary: When a C2 JU originates, reports, receives, assumes reporting responsibility for, or resolves differences concerning identity classification of a surveillance track.
scope.success_boundary: The C2 JU reports and maintains the track's standard identity and permitted identity amplifiers according to the surveillance rules and resolves identity differences through the specified automatic or manual procedures.
in_scope: Standard identity definitions and use in track identity classification
Exercise Track identity restrictions and Identity Amplifying Descriptor handling
Special Interest Indicator as identity amplification
Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and related identity amplification accepted/retransmitted on R2 assumption
Identity reporting for inactive/limited-status interface units
Identity difference recognition, reporting, acceptance, rejection, and operator alerts
Environment/Category and Exercise Indicator conflict processing relative to identity
Use of PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator in identity resolution
Change Data Order (J7.0 ACT=2) identity constraints
out_of_scope: NonC2 JU transmission restrictions except where they constrain received surveillance information
Positional correlation algorithms except identity-related correlation restrictions
Track quality computation except where identity difference procedures interact with R2
Subsurface track reporting responsibility and manual-only correlation except identity field exchange
Electronic warfare product reporting responsibility except identity difference applicability
Network participation group scheduling or detailed word-by-word transmission rules
IFF/SIF code management

evidence.quote: Standard identity is provided in terms of the following definitions:
Only tracks with standard identity of Friend can be modified by the exercise identity.

A track's identity can be further amplified by designating it as a track of special interest. This is accomplished by setting the identity field as appropriate and by setting the special interest indicator.

For each of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields which are implemented by a C2 JU, the JU shall accept all defined field values for retransmission and operator appreciation, in the event of assuming R2 for a previously-reported track.
The exchange of Surveillance data requires procedures to recognize and resolve differences in ID and Environment/Category.
ID differences occur when a JU holds a local ID on a track (local data) which differs from the ID being reported on the interface (remote data).

requirements.text: When classifying a track, the C2 JU shall use the defined standard identities: Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, or Hostile.

evidence.quote: Pending - A track which has not been subjected to the identification process.

Hostile - A track declared to belong to any opposing nation, party, group, or entity, which by virtue of its behavior or information collected on it such as characteristics, origin or nationality contributes to the threat to friendly forces.

requirements.text: The C2 JU may further amplify standard identity using the Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Identity Amplifying Descriptor, Specific Type, Platform, Platform Activity, and Identity Confidence fields as applicable.

evidence.quote: These standard identity terms are further amplified by the Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator and Identity Amplifying Descriptor, Specific Type, Platform, Platform Activity, and Identity Confidence fields.

requirements.text: When the Exercise Indicator is set to value 0, Non-Exercise Track, the C2 JU shall specify the standard identity of the track in the Identity field.
requirements.conditions: {"exercise_indicator":"0"}

evidence.quote: When the Exercise Indicator is set to value 0, Non-Exercise Track, the standard identity of the track shall be specified in the Identity field.

requirements.text: When the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1, Exercise Track, the C2 JU shall set the track's standard identity to Friend and shall specify the exercise identity in the Identity Amplifying Descriptor field.
requirements.conditions: {"exercise_indicator":"1"}

evidence.quote: Exercise Indicator is set to value 1, Exercise Track, the standard identity of the track shall be Friend and the exercise identity shall be specified in the Identity Amplifying Descriptor field.

requirements.text: The C2 JU shall not set the Identity Amplifying Descriptor field unless the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1, Exercise Track.

evidence.quote: The Identity Amplifying Descriptor field shall not be set unless the Exercise Indicator field is set to value 1, Exercise Track.

requirements.text: Only tracks with standard identity Friend shall be modified by the exercise identity.

evidence.quote: Only tracks with standard identity of Friend can be modified by the exercise identity.

requirements.text: When an Exercise Track has Identity Amplifying Descriptor value 6, FAKER, the C2 JU shall identify the track as a friendly track acting as a hostile for exercise purposes.
requirements.conditions: {"exercise_indicator":"1","identity_amplifying_descriptor":"6"}

evidence.quote: a track with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1, Exercise Track, and the Identity Amplifying Descriptor set to value 6, FAKER, shall be identified as a friendly track acting as a hostile for exercise purposes.

requirements.text: When an Exercise Track has Identity Amplifying Descriptor value 5, JOKER, the C2 JU shall identify the track as a friendly track acting as a suspect for exercise purposes.

scope.goal: Define C2 JU requirements for terminating, dropping, and purging surveillance tracks and related surveillance entities on Link 16.
scope.start_boundary: When a C2 JU ceases reporting, drops, correlates away, or locally purges a surveillance track/point/product for which it has or does not have reporting responsibility, or processes a drop report/correlation-related termination.
scope.success_boundary: The C2 JU transmits required J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track Reports only where mandated, suppresses reports for local purges and R2 shifts, and handles termination constraints for air/surface/land, subsurface, ballistic missile, and EW surveillance data.
in_scope: J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report transmission and suppression
purging of remote tracks/points and prohibition on transmitting drop reports for purged entities
termination of air, surface (maritime), and land (ground) track data
termination of subsurface track data and related ASW entities
termination of ballistic missile tracks
termination of EW surveillance product information
correlation/PPLI-triggered drop of surveillance tracks
track number continuity requiring a drop on the old track number
cases where an entity becomes an Active IU and a drop report is prohibited
nonR2 response-message effects on reporting responsibility
disconnecting launch/impact points upon ballistic missile drop
out_of_scope: general surveillance message content unrelated to termination or purging
initial track reporting criteria
full correlation algorithms except where they require a drop report
IFF/SIF update and difference procedures except termination-related effects
filter creation and management except filter-triggered cessation/termination rules
nonC2 JU monitoring requirements except as context for C2 behavior

evidence.visual_region_description: Section 4.4.1 lists point, air, surface, subsurface, land, space/ballistic missile, and EW surveillance data.

evidence.quote:
The JU shall not transmit a 
J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a purged remote track/point.

The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a track 
for which it currently has R2, except in the following cases:
4.4.5.13  TERMINATION OF SUBSURFACE TRACK DATA

Upon transmission or reception of a Drop Track Report for a 
ballistic missile, the JU with R2 of the Launch Point or Impact Point shall 
transmit the Impact Point and/or Launch Point messages with the 
Connect/Disconnect field set to value 1, Disconnect.
4.4.6.17  TERMINATION OF BALLISTIC MISSILE TRACK DATA

4.4.7.6  TERMINATION OF ELECTRONIC WARFARE SURVEILLANCE DATA 
 
The transmission of EW product information shall be terminated when the 
information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not 
met.  The information may be purged in accordance with system design. 
 
When a JU drops or ceases reporting EW information, that it has been 
reporting on the interface, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.  The 
J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted on remote reports.  Remote 
reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU purges a remote track or point, the C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for that purged remote track or point.

evidence.quote: The JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a purged remote track/point.

requirements.text: When a new Track Number is required for a surveillance entity under track number continuity, the C2 JU with R2 shall transmit a Drop Track Report on the old Track Number.

evidence.quote: In cases when a new TN is required, the JU with R2 shall transmit a Drop Track Report on the old TN.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU participating on the Surveillance Network PG correlates a received PPLI report with a track for which that C2 JU has R2, the C2 JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance Track Number.
requirements.conditions: The J7.2 correlation message uses the PPLI Source TN as Retained TN and the surveillance TN as Dropped TN, and the Response Value is set to 1.

evidence.quote: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R2
The C2 JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU ceases reporting a point, line, or area for which it had reporting responsibility, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

evidence.quote: When a JU ceases reporting a point, line, or area for which it had reporting responsibility, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

requirements.text: When dropping a segmented line or multisided area defined by more than one Reference TN, the C2 JU shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for each Reference TN.

evidence.quote: To drop a segmented line or multisided area defined by more than one Reference TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall be transmitted for each Reference TN.

requirements.text: A C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point when the point becomes an Active IU on the interface with the same TN.

evidence.quote: A JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point when the point becomes an Active IU on the interface with the same TN.

requirements.text: A C2 JU that receives a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point, line, or area shall not be required to purge that point, line, or area.

evidence.quote: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point, line, or area shall not be required to purge the point, line, or area.

requirements.text: If a C2 JU does not purge a point, line, or area after receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, it shall assume R2 for the point, line, or area to ensure that it remains active on the interface.

evidence.quote: However, if the JU does not purge a point, line, or area on which it has received a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, it shall assume R2 for the point, line, or area to ensure that it remains active on the interface.

requirements.text: When a remote point, line, or area is purged from a C2 JU by local options, the C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

evidence.quote: When a remote point, line, or area is purged from a system by local options, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.

requirements.text: If a C2 JU fails to receive the terminating J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for an emergency point and receives no further updates, the C2 JU may purge that emergency point after a specified time period has elapsed with no updates.

evidence.quote: If a JU fails to receive the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and further updates are not received, the JU may purge those points after a specified time period has elapsed with no updates.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU ceases reporting an air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) track for which it currently has R2, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, unless an applicable exception suppresses the Drop Track Report.

evidence.quote: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has R2, except in the following cases:

requirements.text: A C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message when it ceases reporting an air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) track because it has relinquished R2 to another JU.

evidence.quote: a. When a JU ceases reporting a track because it has relinquished R2 to another JU.
A J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be sent when a track is no longer being reported due to a shift in R2.

requirements.text: A C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message when an air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.

evidence.quote: b. When that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU receives no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates on a remote air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) track, the C2 JU should have the capability to automatically purge that track after a system-selected specific time interval that considers irregular reporting of nonreal-time tracks.

evidence.quote: There may be cases when a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track.  Each system should have

the capability to automatically purge those tracks after a specific time interval.  The time interval is a system-selected parameter and should consider the irregular reporting of nonreal-time tracks.

requirements.text: When a remote air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) track is automatically purged because no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates were received, the C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

evidence.quote: Under this condition, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU ceases reporting a subsurface track, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, unless that track becomes an active IU on the network with the same address that was previously used as the reference TN.

evidence.quote: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a track except when that track becomes an active IU on the network with the same address as was previously being used as the reference TN.

evidence.quote: For NOTACK areas, Moving Havens, and FWDAs, a J7.0 (ACT=0) message shall be transmitted at time of deactivation.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU receives no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates on a remote subsurface track with DRT 0 through 3, the C2 JU shall have the capability to automatically purge that track after a system-selected time interval.

evidence.quote: Each system will have the capability to automatically purge those tracks (DRT = 0-3) after a specific time interval.  The time interval is a system-selected parameter

requirements.text: When a remote subsurface track with DRT 0 through 3 is automatically purged because no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates were received, the C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

evidence.quote: Under this condition a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.

requirements.text: A C2 JU shall not automatically purge DATUMs with DRT = 4.

evidence.quote: DATUMS (DRT = 4) shall not be purged automatically.

requirements.text: A DATUM shall only be dropped or purged by operator action.

evidence.quote: A DATUM shall only be dropped or purged by operator action.

evidence.quote: Should the inactive IU return to the interface as an Active IU, the JU holding R2 shall cease reporting the IU, but a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU ceases reporting a ballistic missile track for which it currently has R2, it shall transmit a J7.0 Track Management message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0, Drop Track Report, except when it ceases reporting the track because it has relinquished R2 to another JU.

evidence.quote: The J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0, Drop Track Report, is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a ballistic missile track for which it currently has R2, except when a JU ceases reporting a track because it has relinquished R2 to another JU.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU receives no ballistic missile Drop Track Report and no further updates on a remote ballistic missile track, the C2 JU should have the capability to automatically purge that track after a specific system-selected time interval.

evidence.quote: Each system should have the capability to automatically purge those tracks after a specific time interval.  The time interval is a system-selected parameter.

requirements.text: When a C2 JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

evidence.quote: When a JU drops or ceases reporting EW information, that it has been reporting on the interface, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

requirements.text: A C2 JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on remote EW reports.

evidence.quote: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted on remote reports.

requirements.text: A C2 JU may automatically purge remote EW reports based on system criteria.

evidence.quote: Remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.

requirements.text: It is illegal for a C2 JU to assume reporting responsibility for another unit's J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report.

evidence.quote: It is illegal to assume reporting responsibility for another unit's J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report.

requirements.text: J3.7 messages transmitted by nonR2 JUs with the Response Indicator set to value 1 shall not affect reporting responsibility.

evidence.quote: J3.7 messages transmitted by nonR2 JUs with the Response Indicator set to value 1 shall not affect reporting responsibility.

requirements.text: When executing a correlation and the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.

evidence.quote: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message. The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall be transmitted after the J7.2 message.

requirements.text: A C2 JU receiving a J7.2 correlation request and rejecting it shall not interpret the J7.2 message as a Drop Track Message for determining R2 when it holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track.

evidence.quote: C2 JUs rejecting a J7.2 message and holding the Dropped TN as a local or common local track shall not interpret the J7.2 message as a Drop Track message for the purpose of determining R2.

requirements.text: The C2 JU shall transmit the Impact Point and/or Launch Point messages with the Connect/Disconnect field set to value 1 (Disconnect) upon transmission or reception of a Drop Track Report for a ballistic missile, if the C2 JU has R2 of the Launch Point or Impact Point.
requirements.conditions: Drop Track Report transmitted/received for ballistic missile; C2 JU has R2 for related Launch/Impact Point.

evidence.quote: Upon transmission or reception of a Drop Track Report for a ballistic missile, the JU with R2 of the Launch Point or Impact Point shall transmit the Impact Point and/or Launch Point messages with the Connect/Disconnect field set to value 1, Disconnect.

scope.goal: Define the rules and procedures for a C2 JU to assume, relinquish, and maintain Reporting Responsibility (R2) for surveillance tracks and points, ensuring only the unit with the best data reports the track.
scope.start_boundary: Detection or initiation of a track/point, or receipt of remote surveillance data.
scope.success_boundary: The C2 JU correctly holds R2, transmits reports when eligible, relinquishes R2 when required, and assumes R2 from other units according to specific criteria for Air, Surface, Land, Subsurface, Space/Ballistic Missile, and EW tracks.
in_scope: General R2 assignment and retention rules
R2 rules for Air, Surface (Maritime), and Land (Ground) tracks
R2 rules for Point surveillance (Reference, Emergency, Land)
R2 rules for Subsurface (Maritime) tracks
R2 rules for Space and Ballistic Missile tracks
R2 rules for Electronic Warfare (EW) products
Integration of PPLI reports with surveillance R2
Reporting of inactive Interface Units (IUs)
Minimum wait times before transmitting after status change
out_of_scope: Non-C2 JU transmission rules (prohibited from transmitting on Surveillance NPG)
Detailed message format encoding (unless relevant to R2 logic like ACT fields)
Weapons coordination messages (J10 series) except where they impact R2 constraints (OCCs)
Filter management implementation details unrelated to R2 assumption

evidence.quote: Surveillance data reporting is initiated by the JU which first detects or initiates a track/point and makes it available for reporting on the interface. Each track/point initiated and reported shall be assigned a TN from the JU's allocated block. At that time, the JU shall have R2 for the track/point.

R2 procedures for Air, Surface (Maritime), and Land (Ground) tracks are contained in this paragraph. These rules are designed to ensure that only the JU having the best positional data available is reporting the track on the interface.

requirements.text: A C2 JU that first detects or initiates a track or point and makes it available for reporting on the interface shall assign a TN from its allocated block and shall have R2 for that track or point at that time.

requirements.text: When a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message containing the TN is received for a Subsurface (Maritime) track, another JU may report the contact using that TN.

requirements.text: If the C2 JU correlates received PPLI reports with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, it shall accept the PPLI information and disregard the J3 surveillance data, unless Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI is 0.
requirements.conditions: Correlation found with PPLI, another C2 JU has R2, TNs same

target.name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

scope.goal: Exchange IFF and SIF transponder data for surveillance tracks, including surveillance reporting, unique Mode II protection, clearing, difference resolution, update requests, and special code reporting applicable to a C2 JU
scope.start_boundary: When a C2 JU participates in Link 16 surveillance exchange and reports, receives, clears, requests, or resolves IFF/SIF modes and codes associated with surveillance tracks or points
scope.success_boundary: The C2 JU reports IFF/SIF data when it has reporting responsibility, processes remote data and conflicts using the specified management messages and rules, and terminates or clears data only under the specified conditions
in_scope: J3.2/J3.3 IFF/SIF surveillance data reporting by the JU with R2
J7.5 Clear IFF/SIF, Difference Report, Update Request, and Special Code messages
IFF/SIF difference resolution using Table 4.7-5
IFF/SIF reporting on J3.1 and J3.5 points where specified
Unique Mode II Code Protection
Current/noncurrent IFF/SIF data handling
Special code reporting
J3.XC1 transmission timing rules
out_of_scope: General J3 track position, velocity, altitude, track quality, and reporting-responsibility rules not specific to IFF/SIF
PPLI own-unit periodic IFF/SIF reporting in J2 messages, except where received PPLI affects J3 reporting or J7.5 processing
Non-C2 JU data transmission
Track correlation procedures except IFF/SIF-specific Mode II protections

scope.goal: Define requirements for a Non-C2 JU receiving surveillance situational awareness data over the Link 16 Surveillance NPG, including processing of track management, alerts, IFF/SIF, and exercise data.
scope.start_boundary: Monitoring the Surveillance NPG to receive J3-series remote surveillance track and point data.
scope.success_boundary: The Non-C2 JU receives and processes situational awareness, early warning, drop-track, alert, and IFF/SIF data needed for its platform mission, without transmitting on the Surveillance NPG (except where explicitly permitted by Information Management rules).
in_scope: Reception of J3 Surveillance messages (Air, Surface, Subsurface, Land, Space, EW, Reference Points).
Prohibition of transmission on Surveillance NPG.
Processing of Drop Track Reports (J7.0 ACT=0).
Purging of remote tracks.
Handling of Force Tell and Emergency alerts (J2, J3, J7.0).
Handling of Exercise Status Orders (J7.0 ACT=6) and Exercise Indicators.
IFF/SIF data monitoring, difference reporting (J7.5), and update requests.
Filtering rules (Receive filters, override by alerts).
Identity and Environment/Category difference resolution (J7.0 ACT=1, ACT=2).
Strength changes (J7.0 ACT=5).
Track Identifier management (J7.4).
Association data purging (J7.7).
out_of_scope: C2 JU transmission of J3 surveillance messages.
C2 JU reporting responsibility and common tracking procedures (correlation/decorrelation).
Needline PG specific variance reporting (J12.6) unless explicitly tied to general SA reception.
Electronic warfare, ballistic missile covariance, IFF management, filter management, or other C2-specific procedures not applicable to Non-C2 reception.

evidence.quote: NonC2 JUs shall receive situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG including track and Reference Point data necessary to support the platform mission. NonC2 JUs shall not transmit on the Surveillance NPG.
To support their missions, nonC2 JUs shall monitor the Surveillance NPG; however, they are prohibited from transmitting on this NPG.
NonC2 JUs shall process J7.0 messages with the Track Management Action field set to value 0, Drop Track Report, for locally held remote tracks.

These messages are monitored by nonC2 JUs, such as fighter aircraft, for situational awareness and early warning information.

scope.goal: Initiate Emergency Point Reports
scope.start_boundary: When an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts is detected and is to be reported as a J3.1 Emergency Point, or when the operator has additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point.
scope.success_boundary: A J3.1 Emergency Point message is transmitted with required emergency point data and applicable associations; emergency points are updated while active and are normally terminated with J7.0 (ACT = 0) when the emergency ceases.
in_scope: Transmitting emergency points as Link 16 J3.1 messages
Relating emergency points to a previously reported track or point using TN, Previously Reported
Assigning a distinct TN, Reference to the emergency point
Distinguishing exercise emergency-point reports from actual emergencies
Reporting on previously reported emergency points only through operator action when additional or more current information is held
Assuming R2 for an emergency point through operator action under specified loss/inactivity/update-failure conditions
Preserving TN Reference and TN Previously Reported when assuming R2
Including available IFF/SIF Modes I, II, and III data in J3.1 messages
Populating J3.1 IFF/SIF data from the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated
Periodically updating active emergency points
Normally terminating emergency points with J7.0 (ACT = 0) when the emergency ceases
Not using alerts for J3.1 and not filtering J3.1 messages
out_of_scope: Air, surface, subsurface, land, space, ballistic missile, or EW track reporting not specific to emergency points
PPLI reporting procedures for JUs
Detailed J3.1 bit-level encoding or word layout
Specific periodic update interval values not supplied in the excerpts
Network participation group allocation rules beyond emergency-point reporting constraints

evidence.quote:
b.  J3.1  -  Used to report the existence of an emergency condition 
that requires search and rescue efforts.

Emergency points are transmitted as J3.1 messages.  Emergency points may be 
related to a previously reported track/point.  In these cases the J3.1 
message shall contain, as amplifying information, the TN, Previously Reported 
that is associated with the emergency point.  The emergency point shall have 
a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.  When the 
Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the report is for 
exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.

Any JU may report, through operator action only, on a previously reported 
emergency point when that JU has additional or more current information on 
the point.  In addition, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on an 
emergency point, the unit with R2 is declared inactive, or if no periodic 
update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by 
operator action only, assume R2 for the point.  A JU assuming R2 for an 
emergency point shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN 
Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.

IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) are transmitted in the J3.1 and 
J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages when available.  The IFF/SIF data in the J3.1 message 
shall contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track 
for which the emergency point was initiated.

Emergency points are periodically updated and are normally terminated via the 
J7.0 (ACT = 0) message when the emergency ceases.

Alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message since these points 
cannot be filtered.
A J3.1 message shall not be filtered.

scope.goal: Allow the Business Owner to analyze customer purchasing activity through auction admin reports and analytics that reveal customer frequency, sales/conversions, purchasing behavior, value, cancellations, and returns.
scope.start_boundary: The Business Owner accesses reporting or analytics from the Auction Admin Main Menu / Reports menu to examine customer purchasing activity.
scope.success_boundary: The Business Owner can use available reports and analytics to review customer purchasing frequency, monetary activity, items won, sales/conversions, cancellation and return behavior, and customer rankings over selected criteria or timeframes.
in_scope: Auction Admin reports available through the Auction Admin Main Menu
Customer activity reports, RFM reporting, customer ranking reporting, and sales reporting
Omniture and Google Analytics minimum purchasing-related reporting
Report criteria and output fields needed to analyze customer purchasing activity
out_of_scope: Customer-facing bidding, registration, watch list, and current bid pages
Auction creation, scheduling, and event profile administration
Customer service account suspension or deactivation workflows
Second-chance offer processing
Future Phase 2 enhancements beyond the documented reports

scope.goal: Configure Global Auction Rules
scope.start_boundary: The Auctioneer accesses the Auction Admin Manage Global Settings page.
scope.success_boundary: The Auctioneer applies changes to the sitewide reserve/bid-increment, overtime bidding, shipping, and preview rules; reserve and bid-increment defaults may be overridden by Event Profiles where specified.
in_scope: Manage Global Settings page with four sections
Reserve tiers, opening-bid/reserve settings, and bid-increment sitewide defaults
Overtime bidding enablement, extension duration, participant notice, and automatic bid-extension behavior
Sitewide first-item and subsequent-item shipping charges
Preferred-customer revenue threshold, per-item shipping charge, and annual reset
Temporary shipping promotions, date/time validation, duration limit, promotional charge, and apply action
Preview duration, hours/minutes fields, 24-hour maximum, and apply action
out_of_scope: Creating or scheduling individual auctions
Creating or editing Auction Event Profiles themselves
User access management and administrator permissions
Customer account review, suspension, or deactivation
Customer-facing checkout payment processing
Phase 2 international shipping and future enhancements

evidence.quote: 9.5 The Manage Global Settings Page Refer to the page mockup below. This page will have four (4) sections.
9.5.1 Reserve Tier and Bid Increment Sitewide Default Settings Section
9.5.2 Overtime Bidding Section
9.5.3 Shipping Settings Section
9.5.4 Preview Section
Manages the site's global settings, including Bid Extend (“Overtime bidding”) functionality, shipping promos, etc.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall access a Manage Global Settings page containing four sections for configuring sitewide auction settings.

evidence.quote: The Manage Global Settings Page Refer to the page mockup below. This page will have four (4) sections.

requirements.text: The Reserve Tier and Bid Increment Sitewide Default Settings section shall contain user-definable cost tiers, and each cost tier shall have corresponding fields governing the reserve (opening bids) amount and bid increment for all items in that cost tier.

evidence.quote: This section will contain user-definable cost tiers. Each cost tier will have corresponding fields which govern the reserve (opening bids) amount and the bid increment for all items in that cost tier.

requirements.text: Bid-increment fields shall allow only discrete, full dollar amounts.

evidence.quote: The bid increment fields allow for discrete, full dollar amounts.

requirements.text: Global reserve and bid-increment parameters shall be capable of being overridden by Event Profiles.

evidence.quote: These parameters may be overridden by Event Profiles. See the Event Profiles section for details.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall enter the overtime time-extension duration and apply overtime-bidding settings.

evidence.quote: There will be two data fields, where the Auctioneer can enter the duration of the time extension, and a "Apply Changes" button.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall be able to create an overtime time extension of anywhere from 10 seconds to 60 minutes.

evidence.quote: The Auctioneer can create a time extension of anywhere from 10 seconds to 60 minutes.

requirements.text: When overtime bidding is ON, Product Details pages shall notify auction participants with a prominent message stating: "Overtime Bidding is On!"
requirements.conditions: {"when":"Overtime bidding is ON"}

evidence.quote: When overtime bidding is ON, the Product Details pages will notify the auction participants with a prominent message, stating: "Overtime Bidding is On!"

requirements.text: When overtime bidding is ON and a bid is placed before the scheduled end of the auction, the auction shall automatically be extended by the configured duration; if no subsequent bid is placed before that extension ends, the auction shall end.
requirements.conditions: {"when":"Overtime bidding is ON and a bid is placed before scheduled auction end"}

evidence.quote: If User A places a bid five seconds before the scheduled end of the auction, the auction will automatically be extended by 20 seconds. If no one else bids before 20 seconds is over, the auction ends.

requirements.text: When overtime bidding is ON and another user places a subsequent bid before the current extension ends, the auction shall be extended again for the configured duration, and this extension shall repeat for subsequent bids.
requirements.conditions: {"when":"Overtime bidding is ON and another bid is placed before the current extension ends"}

evidence.quote: If another user places a subsequent bid before the extension is over, the auction is extended for yet another 20 seconds, and so on.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall configure the sitewide first item shipping charge and the sitewide subsequent items shipping charge.

evidence.quote: This section contains two fields for setting shipping charges: One for "sitewide first item shipping charge", and a second for "sitewide subsequent items shipping charge."

requirements.text: For shipping-charge purposes, subsequent items shall be items that are won during the same calendar day.

evidence.quote: Subsequent Items are items that are won during the same calendar day.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall configure the Preferred Customer shipping charge by setting the Revenue Threshold to Qualify for Preferred Status and the New Per-Item Shipping Charge.

evidence.quote: There will be a "Preferred Customer" shipping charge. This section allows the Auctioneer to set two values: the "Revenue Threshold to Qualify for Preferred Status" and the "New Per-Item Shipping Charge."

requirements.text: The preferred-customer revenue threshold shall reset to zero for all customers on January 1 each year.

evidence.quote: Revenue threshold re-sets to zero for all customers on January 1 each year.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall set temporary shipping promotions using fields for starting and ending dates and times.

evidence.quote: The Auctioneer will also be able to set temporary shipping promotions. There will be two fields for entering starting and ending dates and times.

requirements.text: The system shall use data validation to ensure temporary shipping-promotion dates are in the future and that the ending date is after the start date.

evidence.quote: Data validation should be used to ensure that the dates are in the future and that the ending date is after the start date.

requirements.text: The system shall prevent a temporary shipping promotion from lasting for more than seven days.

evidence.quote: The system should prevent the promotion from lasting for more than seven days.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall enter the temporary promotional shipping charge and apply shipping-setting changes.

evidence.quote: There will be a field for the Auctioneer to enter the temporary promotional shipping charge. This section should include a button to "Apply Changes."

requirements.text: The Preview section shall determine how soon new items appear online before the system begins accepting bids.

evidence.quote: The preview section determines how soon new items will appear online before the system will begin accepting bids.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall configure preview duration using two fields: one for hours and one for minutes.

evidence.quote: There will be two fields: one for hours, one for minutes.

requirements.text: The maximum amount of time an item can be in Preview status shall be 24 hours.

evidence.quote: The maximum amount of time that an item can be in "Preview" status is 24 hours.

scope.goal: Define requirements for the Auctioneer to view, edit, and remove existing current and scheduled auctions using the View / Edit Current & Scheduled Auctions page.
scope.start_boundary: When the Auctioneer accesses the View / Edit Current & Scheduled Auctions page and searches for currently running or scheduled auctions to edit or remove.
scope.success_boundary: When matching auctions are selected, permitted edits, removals, event-profile applications, or deletions are applied through the page; only Auctioneers may end an auction early or delete an auction.
in_scope: Searching current and scheduled auctions by status, SKU, participant email, scheduled dates, cost range, product type, and duration
Enabling or disabling thumbnail images and executing search
Filtering and rearranging search result columns
Displaying the specified search result columns and initial blank fields
Navigating from Product ID to SKU History
Selecting all results and performing actions on checked/selected items
Removing checked items from an auction
Editing durations, bid increments, and reserve amounts
Applying ending or starting times to all selected items using column-header dropdown lists
Creating a grouping or event
Applying one available event profile to selected items
Displaying Apply Changes and action controls within the specified resolution behavior
Restricting early ending and auction deletion to Auctioneers
Validation of start/end times
out_of_scope: Creating new auctions from the Create New Auctions page
Consumer bidding behavior
Checkout and payment processing
Customer-account suspension or deactivation
General reporting unrelated to the View/Edit page
Managing global settings or event profile creation
Inventory import processes

scope.goal: Define how a Customer Service Representative investigates customer auction inquiries using Customer History and related account, bid, order, payment, note, suspension, deactivation, and Review Status information while preserving restrictions on bid placement.
scope.start_boundary: A Customer Service Representative needs to resolve a customer inquiry or troubleshoot a customer service issue and accesses the Customer History page or customer account data.
scope.success_boundary: The Customer Service Representative can locate the customer, inspect relevant bid, order, account, payment, and note information, and take only supported or authorized account actions such as notes, Review status, code-approved deactivation, or unlocking where the stated non-payment rules permit it.
in_scope: Customer History page access for troubleshooting customer service issues
Searching customers by email, phone number, or customer name
Displaying customer identity/contact results and action buttons
Viewing method of payment, account notes, order history, and bid history
Suspending or deactivating accounts subject to code authorization
Handling customer complaints and concerns
Accessing and editing customer information and customer accounts
Researching bidding issues and entering account notes
Removing bids only in emergency circumstances
Unlocking or removing accounts from Review Status under the stated rules
Prohibition on placing bids for customers
Non-payment and escalation constraints that affect CSR handling of auction inquiries
Using the designated Customer Service email account
out_of_scope: Auctioneer scheduling and global auction settings
Endeca navigation design
Customer-facing registration and checkout page design
General reporting unrelated to a specific customer inquiry
Phase 2 and future enhancements such as international functionality, third-party vendors, SMS notifications, or chat
Creating new accounts

scope.goal: Define the Auctioneer's requirements for managing users authorized to access the Auction Administration application, including UAM pages, listing, creating, editing, deleting users, assigning Administrator or User access, and granting User-level permissions.
scope.start_boundary: The Auctioneer opens User Access Management from the Administration Menu on the Auction Administration Main Menu.
scope.success_boundary: Administration users are listed and can be created, edited, or deleted, with access level and permissions saved according to the stated controls.
in_scope: User Access Management menu option and UAM page structure
UAM front page with List All Users and Create New User
Listing all Auction Administration application users
Creating and editing Auction Administration users
Deleting Auction Administration users with confirmation
Assigning Administrator or User access
Granting User-level permissions for auctions and customer account deactivation/review
Password fields and required password change setting
Customer review-status effects because the source ties them to the grantable UAM permission
out_of_scope: Customer-facing registration and customer sign-in flows
Customer history page functions other than effects of permissions granted in UAM
Auction scheduling, event profiles, inventory, reporting, checkout, shipping, and payment processing
Third-party vendor portal access in future enhancements

evidence.quote: User Access Management (UAM) will be an option on the Administration Menu from the Auction Administration Main Menu.

There will be three pages for UAM. The first is a very simple page with only two buttons/links: 1) List All Users; and 2) Create New User. The second page is the “List All Users” page. The third page is the “Create or Edit User” page.
This page will list all users authorized to use the auction administration application. Columns will include Last Name, First Name, (Job) Title, Login ID, Admin, Delete, and Edit.
This page is accessed when the user chooses either: 1) the “Create New User” button on the UAM front page, or 2) the “Edit” button on the “List All Users” page.

target.name: Respond to a Second-Chance Purchase Offer

scope.goal: Define the Customer's actions and resulting system behavior when receiving and responding to an automated 2nd-Chance purchase offer after a PayPal or Amazon Payments winner's unpaid order is cancelled and the item is placed on hold.
scope.start_boundary: An automated 2nd-Chance email is sent to the second-place finisher after cancellation of the original winner's unpaid PayPal or Amazon Payments order, provided eligibility conditions are met.
scope.success_boundary: The customer accepts the offer by credit card or PayPal/Amazon Payments and the resulting order is generated for shipment or payment, or declines/does not respond so the item is returned to auction available inventory.
in_scope: 2nd-Chance offer trigger and offer price
Three-day/72-hour response window
Credit-card acceptance option
PayPal or Amazon Payments acceptance option and sign-in/payment routing
Decline option
No-response outcome
Eligibility restrictions tied to bid cost and fraud prevention
out_of_scope: Auction Admin 2nd-Chance reporting contents
General auction scheduling
Original auction winner checkout process
International shipping future enhancements
Other future Phase 2 enhancements

evidence.quote: When auction participants who have PayPal or Amazon Payments set as their default Method of Payment, they are required to pay for their winnings within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time. When they do not, those orders will be cancelled and the item placed into a “hold” status.

When these orders are cancelled, it will trigger an automated email, which will go to the second-place finisher, if there is one. This email will offer to sell the item to the 2nd-place finisher at their last bid price. It will give the email recipient three options:

scope.goal: Define Customer Service Representative actions and business rules for restoring bidding privileges after a customer's PayPal or Amazon Payments auction winnings remain unpaid and the resulting order cancellation places the account in Review Status.
scope.start_boundary: A PayPal or Amazon Payments customer has unpaid auction winnings older than the 7-day/168-hour payment window, the expired order is automatically cancelled, and the system places or has placed the account in Review Status, which blocks bidding.
scope.success_boundary: A Customer Service Representative removes the eligible account from Review Status, subject to the required credit-card update and escalation-policy restrictions, so the customer may bid again when permitted.
in_scope: System-imposed Review Status and bidding block after expired PayPal or Amazon Payments auction winnings
CSR-only unlocking of Review Status accounts
Limitation that customers cannot self-unlock by paying cancelled orders
Ordinary unlock eligibility tied to up to three nonpayment cancellations
Payment-obligation reminder when eligible customers contact the call center
Escalation policy after more than three nonpayments in twelve months, subject to the 10 percent exception
CSR removal of Review Status after escalation based on account update with a credit card
Restriction on using PayPal or Amazon Payments until the order cancellation rate falls below 10 percent
Customer History order-history support for CSR troubleshooting restoration
out_of_scope: Initial bidding process and bid placement UI
Payment processing before the seven-day deadline
Automated payment processing administration
Customer self-service unlocking
Second-chance offer workflow

Phase 2 international functionality

evidence.quote: Customers / Bidders who have unresolved (i.e., unpaid) auction winnings greater than 7 days old will not be allowed to bid. The system will automatically lock accounts when a PayPal or Amazon Payments customer allows their order(s) to expire, thus putting the account into a "Review Status." These "Review Status" accounts can only be "unlocked" by a customer service representative. Customers cannot unlock the account themselves by paying for the orders, because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours), so that this product may be returned to the inventory pool and re-auctioned.

Customers who have had orders cancelled can have Customer Service Reps unlock their accounts if they haven't paid up to three times. When these customers contact the call center, they will simply be reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay.

When an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status. The only way for a customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card. They may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.

These customers will be subject to the escalation policy if they fail to pay for auction winnings more than three times in a twelve-month period, unless three times is less than 10% of their total winnings.

The “Order History” section should include order dates , auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU) numbers, order amounts (includes shipping/tax), and status, even if the order was cancelled. Cancelled orders should appear in RED.

scope.goal: Define requirements for the Auctioneer to search for eligible auction product, configure or apply profiles, set scheduling parameters and durations, and create new auction events on the Create New Auctions page.
scope.start_boundary: The Auctioneer opens the Create New Auctions page and searches or selects auction product to schedule.
scope.success_boundary: A new auction event is created for the selected items with valid applied or manually entered auction parameters and schedule.
in_scope: Create New Auctions page general requirements
Search section capabilities (filters, wildcards, cost range)
Search results display, columns, and actions (filtering, sorting, bulk actions)
Manual and event-profile-driven auction parameter configuration
Auction duration selection (standard and manual)
Validation rules (start/end times, inventory eligibility, overlapping quantities)
Auto-scheduler capability
out_of_scope: Editing currently running or already scheduled auctions after creation (Section 9.9)
Customer-facing bidding behavior
Global settings and event profile administration (creation/editing of profiles themselves)
Checkout, payment processing, shipping, reporting outputs

evidence.quote: 9.8 The Create New Auctions Page

The Auction Merchandiser/Scheduler (the “Auctioneer”) will use this page on a daily basis to 
schedule new auctions.

requirements.text: The Auctioneer shall use the Create New Auctions page on a daily basis to schedule new auctions.

evidence.quote:
The Auction Merchandiser/Scheduler (the “Auctioneer”) will use this page on a daily basis to 
schedule new auctions.

requirements.text: The platform shall not be limited to hourly closing times for new auctions.

evidence.quote: The platform will NOT be limited to hourly closing times!

requirements.text: The scheduling system shall allow the Auctioneer to schedule auctions far into the future, at least one month ahead.

evidence.quote: Need to be able to schedule far into the future (at least a month).

requirements.text: The scheduling application shall never allow the Auctioneer to create an auction with the same starting and ending date/time.

evidence.quote: The scheduling application should never allow the Auctioneer to create an auction with the same starting & ending date / time.

requirements.text: The search section shall enable the Auctioneer to find product for scheduling.

evidence.quote: This section enables the Auctioneer to find product for scheduling.

scope.goal: Define Customer Service Representative capabilities and constraints for suspending customers in Review status, deactivating customer accounts, and unlocking/removing accounts from Review Status after non-payment or escalation.
scope.start_boundary: A CSR identifies a customer account to suspend, deactivate, or unlock through customer contact, the customer’s request, evidence of fraudulent/undesirable activity, or the account’s Review Status.
scope.success_boundary: The customer account is placed in Review Status, permanently deactivated with required approval/code, or removed from Review Status according to the stated conditions, and the customer’s ability to bid or use payment methods reflects that state.
in_scope: CSR suspension of auction customers by placing accounts in Review Status
Effects of Review Status on sign-in, account settings, bidding, and order generation
Permanent deactivation of bidding rights and manager/supervisor code approval
Customer History tool capabilities used by CSRs for suspension/deactivation
CSR unlocking or removal of accounts from Review Status after cancelled or expired PayPal/Amazon Payments orders
Restrictions that customers cannot unlock their own Review Status accounts by paying cancelled orders
Escalation policy thresholds and restrictions on future PayPal or Amazon Payments use
out_of_scope: Auctioneer scheduling and global settings
CSR placement of bids on behalf of customers
Customer self-service unlock by payment for cancelled orders
Routine payment gateway integration outside the account lock/escalation rules
Auction creation, editing, or deletion
International shipping and Phase 2 enhancements

target.name: Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points

scope.goal: Define requirements for a C2 JU to associate and correlate related surveillance tracks and points, including PPLI integration, air/surface track correlation/decorrelation, dual designation resolution, subsurface association, ballistic missile correlation, and EW product correlation.
scope.start_boundary: Receipt of surveillance data (J3 messages), PPLI reports (J2 messages), or local sensor detection initiating a track/point.
scope.success_boundary: Tracks and points are correctly correlated, associated, or decorrelated; dual designations are resolved via J7.2 messages or operator action; and reporting responsibility (R2) is managed according to correlation outcomes.
in_scope: Integration of PPLI reports with surveillance data
Air and Surface track correlation and decorrelation
Resolution of Air and Surface track dual designations
Subsurface track association
Ballistic missile track correlation
EW product information correlation
Point-to-point and track-to-point association rules
out_of_scope: NonC2 JU correlation capabilities (except where explicitly required for reception)
Detailed message formatting beyond field usage for correlation logic
Voice coordination procedures (except as a fallback for resolution)

evidence.quote: PPLI data available from J2 messages shall be used by C2 JUs to reduce the redundancy of surveillance track reporting.

There is no interface track-to-point or point-to-point correlation and the 
J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate one track/point with any other 
point.  The J7.7 message shall be used to indicate any association between a 
track/point and another track/point.

In order for common 
tracking to function properly, all C2 JUs shall perform correlation and 
decorrelation of their local track data with respect to the remote data which 
they are receiving.

Instead, it is the function of 
the operator to perform manual correlation of Subsurface surveillance data.  
In order to provide for a complete compilation of the subsurface situation, 
the J7.7 Track Association message is used whenever it is determined that two 
Track Numbers (TNs) are being used to report information for the same target.

To accomplish this, each C2 JU must continuously 
correlate locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile 
tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.

The J7.2 message 
may be used to correlate EW AOPs with surveillance tracks, but shall not be 
used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks.

requirements.text: A C2 JU shall use the J7.7 message to indicate any association between a track or point and another track or point.

evidence.quote: The J7.7 message shall be used to indicate any association between a track/point and another track/point.

requirements.text: A C2 JU shall not use the J7.2 message to correlate one track or point with any other point because there is no interface track-to-point or point-to-point correlation.

evidence.quote: There is no interface track-to-point or point-to-point correlation and the J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate one track/point with any other point.

requirements.text: When an emergency point is related to a previously reported track or point, the C2 JU shall include the TN, Previously Reported associated with the emergency point as amplifying information in the J3.1 message.
